Concept: Erosion Exposure = Assets/Population within erosion threat zone. Unlike flood exposure (area-based), erosion exposure is proximity-based — assets within a documented threat distance of active erosion sites are considered exposed. Steps: Step 1: Confirm all upstream layers CLEAN. Step 2: Apply BUF003 (100m buffer around active erosion sites from G26) to define threat zone. Step 3: Identify assets (G19 infrastructure; G16 roads; G17 buildings; G03 communities) within threat zone. Step 4: Supplement with G27 hotspot zones where site density permits. Step 5: Per community: count exposed assets by type. Step 6: Compute IND06 erosion component. Step 7: Aggregate to community/LGA/state. Step 8: Update DB06 Erosion_Exposure field for validated items. Step 9: Publish CLEAN layer.
G26 (CLEAN — erosion sites), G27 (CLEAN where available), G19 (CLEAN — field infrastructure), G03 (CLEAN — communities), G16 (CLEAN — roads), G17 (CLEAN — buildings)
G32 (exposure index — erosion component), G35 (composite risk), IND06 (infrastructure exposure — erosion component)

Erosion exposure uses proximity-based logic (buffer BUF003 = 100m from active sites) rather than G24-style area overlay. Only Activity_Status = Active erosion sites from G26 are used for the primary threat buffer — inactive and stabilised sites contribute to historical context only. G27 hotspot zones used as supplementary exposure indicator where site density permits hotspot analysis. Threat buffer distance (BUF003 = 100m) must not be changed without updating BUFFER_RULES.csv and re-running the analysis.
